transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2025-04-09
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 57 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Menon (Redwood SE), Olivia Grant (FairWave Director of AI), Marcus Huang (FairWave SRE), Eleanor Park (FairWave Head of Data)

Summary (auto): Quick scoping to align on success criteria and commercial guardrails for a pilot. Capture workloads and schedule benchmarks; confirm credit offer and procurement path.

[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, this is Jordan from Redwood, i'm the AE on the account, and with me is Priya, our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:05] Olivia Grant: Good thanks, hi Jordan, hi Priya, Olivia here. We had a quick preface - we're looking to validate inference economics and latency for our personalization API.
[00:12] Marcus Huang: Marcus here, will be helping with infra and the test VPC.
[00:15] Priya Menon: Great. Goal for today is to agree on success criteria (latency p95, throughput), finalize the pilot credit and commercial guardrails, and determine who provides what artifacts for the benchmarks.
[00:22] Eleanor Park: Sounds good. Our timeline is we want results to inform procurement by end of May, so ideally the pilot runs mid-late April for 3-6 weeks.
[00:30] Jordan Lee: Perfect; that fits our standard pilot cadence. For commercial guardrails we've historically offered a credit-based pilot - for example, a $10k- $25k Redwood credit depending on scope, with a 4-6 week window and usage caps to avoid surprise overages. Priya, feel free to add.
[00:45] Priya Menon: Yup. From a technical perspective we need sample traffic: QPS, average tokens per request, peak concurrency, and a few representative prompt patterns. For benchmarking we run two passes: correctness (quality regression evals on your test prompts) and performance (throughput/latency with production-like traces). We'll run hosted first and optionally Dedicated/VPC if you want to test privately.
[01:05] Olivia Grant: For success criteria we care about p95 latency under 200ms for single-turn personalization calls, and end-to-end 99th percentile SLA under 500ms is a stretch goal. Cost per 1k tokens needs to be within our budget target - we're aiming for $0.20 per 1k tokens equivalent for our 3B-ish model workloads.
[01:25] Marcus Huang: To size things, typical QPS is 12 steady-state and peaks to 120 for flash sales. Avg tokens per request is 150 tokens, sometimes up to 600 for extended contexts.
[01:36] Priya Menon: Good detail, that helps. For the benchmark run we'll need two traffic profiles: steady and spike. We'll also run KV cache warmup scenarios to measure token-latency tradeoffs.
[01:47] Jordan Lee: On commercial guardrails: we propose the following for this pilot - a $15k Redwood credit, 6-week duration, a soft usage cap at 120% of forecasted tokens with an alert to stop, and a mutual evaluation clause: if the POC meets the agreed success criteria, we'll provide a path to direct contracting with discounts layered by committed spend. That is, you can take credits -> PO -> Reserved capacity if you want.
[02:12] Olivia Grant: Is the credit refundable or applied to future invoices?
[02:15] Jordan Lee: Typically credits are applied to your Redwood account and can be applied against future billing in a purchase contract; for pilots they act as an offset during the pilot and can roll into committed spend if you sign a reserved capacity contract. We'll detail that in the commercial term sheet.
[02:28] Marcus Huang: Legal will want to know about data residency and encryption. We are SOC 2 in progress but need to ensure logs, KV cache, and any persisted artifacts from evaluation are not retained beyond the pilot.
[02:40] Priya Menon: Redwood supports private deployments and VPC tunnels; for hosted pilots we can agree on retention windows and KMS for key management. We'll record exactly which logs are kept; we can also run the pilot in your VPC if you prefer - that requires some lead time to provision but is doable within the timeline.
[02:58] Eleanor Park: Procurement question: what's the path after pilot for contracting? We have a standard PO process and legal review, typically 4-6 weeks.
[03:06] Jordan Lee: The usual path: pilot credit agreement or SOW -> performance acceptance based on success criteria -> deal team builds a term sheet -> PO or contract negotiation. For enterprise deals we do an SOW + master services agreement (MSA), and often customers use a PO referencing the signed MSA. We'll work with your procurement to align timelines.
[03:24] Olivia Grant: Can you share the benchmark template and a runbook for the test so our SREs can prep env?
[03:29] Priya Menon: Absolutely. I'll share a benchmark template (CSV + scripts), a runbook for warmup, and sample JMeter / Locust load files. Expect that by Monday 2025-04-13.
[03:40] Marcus Huang: For the VPC option, we'll need a list of IPs and a certificate exchange. How long does that setup usually take?
[03:45] Priya Menon: Typically 3-10 business days depending on approvals; plan on the longer end if you need internal security reviews. For hosted tests it's immediate with token-based creds.
[03:55] Jordan Lee: On metrics we'll measure average latency, p95, p99, throughput (req/sec), tokens/sec, and cost per 1k tokens during the run. We'll also run qualitative evaluation on a held-out test set for hallucination/accuracy.
[04:10] Eleanor Park: For the correctness gate, we want a simple pass/fail: no more than a 5% drop in our key metric (ctr predicted vs actual) on the evaluation set, and manual review for critical flows.
[04:18] Priya Menon: Noted. We'll include that as an acceptance criteria item.
[04:22] Jordan Lee: Any competitors in consideration? Olivia?
[04:26] Olivia Grant: We're evaluating OpenAI for hosted simplicity, also looking at Anthropic and a managed infra partner (ManagedCloudAI) but Redwood's clarity on dedicated capacity and cost controls is compelling.
[04:36] Jordan Lee: Good to know. We'll make sure the benchmark sheet compares apples-to-apples (same prompts, same prompts tokens).

-- mid-call clarifying Q&A --
[22:10] Marcus Huang: Quick note on traffic: our traffic includes many small requests with high QPS so batching and caching performance matters. Will you simulate that?
[22:18] Priya Menon: Yes, we can configure continuous batching and cache scenarios to mimic your small-request profile; we'll also test with kv-cache warm and cold.
[22:25] Olivia Grant: For the pilot credit, what's the mechanism for overspend if we exceed the cap? We need a safety net.
[22:30] Jordan Lee: We'll set a soft cap and an automated alert. Beyond that, we require explicit sign-off to continue at customer's expense. We'll include that in the term sheet.

-- near end recap --
[48:10] Jordan Lee: Recap: Jordan to send commercial term sheet and pilot credit offer ($15k, 6 weeks) by 2025-04-10; Priya to share benchmark templates and runbook by 2025-04-13; FairWave provides sample traces and tokens profile by 2025-04-11; schedule bench run week of 2025-04-21; procurement path: SOW -> MSA -> PO. Any other questions?
[48:35] Olivia Grant: No, that covers it. We'll coordinate internally on sample data and respond with availability for the week of 4/21.
[48:45] Marcus Huang: I'll kick off the VPC ticket and notify Priya when ready.
[48:50] Eleanor Park: Looking forward to the benchmark results.
[48:55] Jordan Lee: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with notes and the term sheet.
